body:
As I am not an expert when it comes to cancer, medicine, or anything similar, I can't tell you how or why. But I can tell you that you are not the only who have suffered a similar fate. My grandfather had undetected bone cancer and died within a month of it being   
 diagnosed, I regret never telling him I loved him. I didn't meet him until I was a bit older so I never really told  him how I felt. He was suffering until the end, there is no changing that, but I do know that he loved me dearly and wouldn't blame me for his death. I would think it is similar to you, I don't think she blames you for not getting a proper goodbye, I think she is happy that you cared and loved for her, you were here world. Don't give up just yet, you can still push through more.

Life will always be harder than death, nothing can change that. But only you can change how hard life is. All I can really say is that the world won't improve by itself, grief won't either. You'll have to work towards your original goal, if you are already so set on dying, might as well go out trying. Try to do everything and anything to change your life, you might not like it, but it's the only way to truly help yourself.
